hints.content:
###Graphing the first point

To graph a line, we need to find two points that are on it. Then we can drag the movable points to those points.

We already have one point, $(-4, -6)$, and we can use the slope of the line to find another point.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The point negative four, negative six is plotted and labeled.

hints.content:
###Use the slope to graph another point

We want the slope to be $-3$:

$\text{slope}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{rise}}}{\maroonD{\text{run}}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\Delta y}}{\maroonD{\Delta x}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{-3}}{\maroonD{1}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{3}}{\maroonD{-1}}$

Starting at $(-4, -6)$, we don't have room on the given grid to go $3$ units down and $1$ unit right. So let's go $\purpleD{3\text{ units up}}$ and $\maroonD{1\text{ unit to the left}}$ to plot another point on the line:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The points negative four, negative six and negative five, negative three are plotted and labeled. There is a vertical dotted segment from negative four, negative six to negative four, negative three that is labeled three. There is a horizontal dotted segment from negative four, negative three to negative five, negative three that is labeled negative one.

question.content:
**Graph a line with a slope of $-3$ that contains the point $(-4, -6)$.**
